# Columns, TAB-separated: id, file, needle, replacement, note. The needle must occur exactly once in the file
# (substring occurrences, overlapping ones included); in needle and replacement \t, \n and \\ are decoded; the
# At least one mutant per clause of the reader; the note names the rule. Not listed, with the reason:
# - B9 (`<<` in arithmetic is a shift): the arithmetic context has no redirection branch to mutate.
# - B12 (a word grows by runs, not per character): a mutant changes only the time, which no test asserts
#   (the PR measures the four 100 KB shapes instead).
# - `w_plain` on the git/gh command word and the "no expansion in the last four characters" of a path to
#   git: no word has the text `git`, `gh` or a `/git` ending made of an expansion's characters (an expansion
#   keeps its `$` source text), so these mutants are equivalent.
# - env's "no expansion in the NAME of NAME=value": a name part with an expansion keeps its `$` source text, which
#   the assignment pattern never matches, so dropping the check is equivalent.
# - the owner-prefix strip of a `gh api … head=owner:branch` value: the shell side strips `owner:` again before it
#   resolves the branch, so dropping the reader's strip is equivalent.
# - separate flags for the quote and the brace regions of one ${…}: the quote region is only under a DQ or HDATA
#   and the brace region only outside one, so the two never meet in one ${…}.
# - the body line scan's stop at a BQ's backtick, and resuming right after a delimiter line the backtick cut: past
#   that backtick line_end() reads every line as empty (substr with a negative length is "" on macOS awk, busybox
#   awk and mawk, checked; a line past it can only match an empty delimiter, which is quoted, so its body is skipped)
#   and at_limit() resumes right after the backtick, so both are equivalent (the stop saves the scan to the end).
# - where a SUB/BQ's first segment starts (right after its opener, or at it): the opener's `$(`, `<(`, `>(` or
#   backtick can never complete a `git` or `gh` in the scope text, so it is equivalent.
# - the hook's fast exit for a command with no `g`: no rule can fire without git or gh in the text, so removing it
# - B15 (a) and the candidate-line clauses of B14: no candidate tag is registered yet.
